clusters.name: Schizoaffective Disorder
items: Major mood episode concurrent with Criterion A of schizophrenia (DSM p.121)
≥2 weeks of delusions or hallucinations without a major mood episode during lifetime duration (DSM p.121)
Mood episode symptoms present for the majority of total active and residual illness duration (DSM p.121-122)

clusters.name: Schizophreniform Disorder
items: Criterion A of schizophrenia met (≥2 of delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized/catatonic behavior, negative symptoms) (DSM p.111)
Illness duration between 1 month and 6 months (DSM p.111)
Impaired social/occupational functioning is NOT required (DSM p.111)

clusters.name: Brief Psychotic Disorder
items: ≥1 positive psychotic symptom: delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized/catatonic behavior (DSM p.108)
Negative symptoms are explicitly EXCLUDED from Criterion A (DSM p.108)
Duration from 1 day to less than 1 month with eventual full return to premorbid functioning (DSM p.108)

clusters.name: Delusional Disorder
items: ≥1 delusion persisting for 1 month or longer (DSM p.104)
Criterion A for schizophrenia has never been met (DSM p.104)
Psychosocial functioning is not markedly impaired apart from delusion impacts (DSM p.105)

criteria.thresholds: Schizoaffective: ≥2 weeks isolated psychosis + mood present majority of illness; Schizophreniform: 1-6 months; Brief Psychotic: 1 day to 1 month; Delusional: ≥1 month delusions
subtypes: Schizoaffective: Bipolar type, Depressive type (DSM p.121)
Schizophreniform: With good prognostic features, Without good prognostic features (DSM p.111)
Brief Psychotic: With marked stressor(s), Without marked stressor(s), With peripartum onset, With catatonia (DSM p.109)
Delusional: Erotomanic, Grandiose, Jealous, Persecutory, Somatic, Mixed, Unspecified, With bizarre content (DSM p.105)

epidemiology.prevalence: Schizoaffective ~0.3% (DSM p.124); Delusional ~0.2% (DSM p.106); Brief Psychotic ~2%-7% of first-onset psychoses (DSM p.110); Schizophreniform ~1/5 of schizophrenia incidence in high-income countries (DSM p.112)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: Schizoaffective: F > M for depressive type (DSM p.124); Brief Psychotic: F > M (Synopsis ch.5); Delusional: overall F = M, Jealous type M > F (DSM p.106); Schizophreniform: M > F (Synopsis ch.5)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: Schizoaffective: early adulthood (DSM p.123); Schizophreniform: adolescents and young adults (Synopsis ch.5); Brief Psychotic: mid-30s average (DSM p.110); Delusional: middle to late adulthood (Synopsis ch.5)
epidemiology.heritability: High familial polygenic risk score (PRS) overlap with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder (DSM p.113, p.124-125)
comorbidities: Substance use disorders (Cannabis, Alcohol, Stimulants) (DSM p.125, p.129)
Personality disorders (Borderline, Schizotypal, Paranoid) (DSM p.111, Synopsis ch.5)
epidemiology.prognosis: Schizoaffective: 5% lifetime suicide risk, prognosis between schizophrenia and mood disorders (DSM p.124-125); Schizophreniform: 1/3 recover, 2/3 convert to schizophrenia/schizoaffective (DSM p.113); Brief Psychotic: >50% relapse (DSM p.110)

etiology.genetic: Elevated polygenic risk scores (PRS) across schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and MDD loci (DSM p.124-125)
etiology.neurobiology: Mesolimbic D2 hyperfunction (positive symptoms), Mesocortical D1/D2 hypofunction (negative/cognitive symptoms), NMDA receptor hypofunction on GABA interneurons (StahlNeuro p.141, p.147-148)
etiology.environmental: Severe psychosocial stressors, trauma, migration, urbanicity, cannabis abuse (DSM p.109-110, p.129, Dulcan p.405)

first_line: Second-Generation Antipsychotics (SGAs): Risperidone (13+ yo), Aripiprazole (13+ yo), Quetiapine, Olanzapine (13+ yo), Lurasidone (13+ yo with ≥350 kcal meal) (Dulcan p.399-401, StahlKids p.40, p.301-302, p.360, p.435)
Psychosocial interventions, CBT, and family psychoeducation (Dulcan p.400-401)
second_line: Mood Stabilizers (Lithium 7+ yo, Valproate) for Schizoaffective Bipolar type (Dulcan p.399, StahlKids p.292, p.475)
Clozapine for treatment-resistant psychosis (Dulcan p.420, StahlKids p.151)
SSRI add-on for persistent depression in Schizoaffective Depressive type (StahlKids p.179)
key_side_effects: Metabolic syndrome, weight gain, dyslipidemia (highest with Olanzapine/Clozapine) (Dulcan p.418, StahlKids p.360)
Akathisia and activation (Aripiprazole, Lurasidone) (StahlKids p.40, p.301)
Agranulocytosis and seizure threshold reduction (Clozapine) (StahlKids p.151)
treatment.monitoring: ANC monitoring for Clozapine (weekly 0-6 mo, biweekly 6-12 mo, monthly thereafter; baseline ANC ≥1500/µL) (StahlKids p.151, p.163); Metabolic panel, BMI, prolactin, lipid/glucose (Dulcan p.418)

items: K-SADS-PL (semi-structured interview for school-age children and adolescents 6-18 yo) (Dulcan p.228, p.278, p.300)
PAPA (Preschool Age Psychiatric Assessment for ages 2-5) (Dulcan p.228)
DSM-5 Level 1 Cross-Cutting Symptom Measure (screen threshold ≥1 Slight for psychosis) (DSM p.843-846)
Clinician-Rated Dimensions of Psychosis Symptom Severity (8 domains rated 0-4) (DSM p.851-853)
Attenuated Psychosis Syndrome (Section III research criteria: ≥1 attenuated symptom ≥1/week for 1 month, starting/worsening past year) (DSM p.903-907)
key_numbers: 8 primary domains in Clinician-Rated Dimensions of Psychosis Severity (DSM p.852)
1/week frequency threshold for Attenuated Psychosis Syndrome (DSM p.903)
34.9% 10-year cumulative transition rate from Attenuated Psychosis to full psychosis (DSM p.906)
73% of converted Attenuated Psychosis cases develop Schizophrenia spectrum disorder (DSM p.906)

items: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (acute psychosis, dysautonomia, oro-facial dyskinesia) (Dulcan p.249, p.406)
PANDAS/PANS (abrupt onset OCD, tics, psychosis following infection) (Dulcan p.379, p.428)
Cannabis-Induced Psychotic Disorder (44% conversion rate to schizophrenia/bipolar) (DSM p.129-130, Dulcan p.405)
PCP / Hallucinogen-Induced Psychosis (NMDA blockade, vertical nystagmus, catatonia) (DSM p.129, StahlNeuro p.141)
Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (TLE) and brain tumors (visual/olfactory hallucinations) (DSM p.132, Dulcan p.397)
Endocrine and metabolic disorders (Cushing's disease, Thyroid dysfunction, Wilson's disease, Porphyria) (DSM p.132)
key_numbers: 44% conversion rate from cannabis-induced psychosis to schizophrenia or bipolar disorder (DSM p.129-130)
≥350 calories required for Lurasidone administration to ensure absorption (StahlKids p.301-302)
4 weeks onset window for 'With good prognostic features' specifier in Schizophreniform (DSM p.111)

high_yield: Schizoaffective disorder requires ≥2 weeks of delusions or hallucinations in the absence of a major mood episode during the lifetime course (DSM p.121).
Schizoaffective Criterion C in DSM-5-TR requires major mood episode symptoms to be present for the majority of the active and residual illness duration (DSM p.121-122).
Schizophreniform disorder lasts between 1 and 6 months; two-thirds of cases convert to Schizophrenia or Schizoaffective disorder (DSM p.111, p.113).
Brief Psychotic disorder lasts between 1 day and 1 month with eventual full return to premorbid functioning; negative symptoms are explicitly excluded from Criterion A (DSM p.108).
Delusional disorder requires ≥1 delusion for ≥1 month without meeting Criterion A for Schizophrenia or causing marked functional impairment (DSM p.104-105).
Lurasidone MUST be administered with at least 350 calories of food to ensure adequate bioavailability (StahlKids p.301-302).
Clozapine ANC monitoring protocol requires baseline ANC ≥1500/µL, weekly testing for 6 months, biweekly for months 6-12, and monthly thereafter (StahlKids p.151, p.163).
